entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv14602"/><div sID="gen28230" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv14602"/><hi type="bold">8. the lord--</hi>evidently the steward's lord, so called in <reference osisRef="Luke.16.3">Lu 16:3</reference>, <reference osisRef="Luke.16.5">5</reference>.<div eID="gen28230" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen28231" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">commended, &c.--</hi>not for his "injustice," but "because he had done wisely," or prudently; with commendable foresight and skilful adaptation of means to end.<div eID="gen28231" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen28232" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">children of this world--</hi>so <reference osisRef="Luke.20.34">Lu 20:34</reference>; compare <reference osisRef="Ps.17.14">Psa 17:14</reference> ("their portion in this life"); <reference osisRef="Phil.3.19">Php 3:19</reference> ("mind earthly things"); <reference osisRef="Ps.4.6">Psa 4:6</reference>, <reference osisRef="Ps.4.7">7</reference>.<div eID="gen28232" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen28233" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">their generation--</hi>or "for their generation"--that is, for the purposes of the "world" they are "of." The greater wisdom (or shrewdness) of the one, in adaptation of means to ends, and in energetic, determined prosecution of them, is none of it for God and eternity--a region they were never in, an atmosphere they never breathed, an undiscovered world, an unborn existence to them--but all for the purposes of their own grovelling and fleeting generation.<div eID="gen28233" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen28234" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">children of light--</hi>(so <reference osisRef="John.12.36">Joh 12:36</reference>; <reference osisRef="Eph.5.8">Ep 5:8</reference>; <reference osisRef="1Thess.5.5">1Th 5:5</reference>). Yet this is only "as night-birds see better in the dark than those of the day owls than eagles" [Cajetan and Trench]. But we may learn lessons from them, as our Lord now shows, and "be wise as serpents." <div eID="gen28234" type="x-p"/>

Yet this is only "as night-birds see better in the dark than those of the day owls than eagles" [Cajetan and Trench]. But we may learn lessons from them, as our Lord now shows, and "be wise as serpents."

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv14603"/><div sID="gen28235" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv14603"/><hi type="bold">9. Make ... friends of--</hi>Turn to your advantage; that is, as the steward did, "by showing mercy to the poor" (<reference osisRef="Dan.4.27">Da 4:27</reference>; compare <reference osisRef="Luke.12.33">Lu 12:33</reference>; <reference osisRef="Luke.14.13">14:13</reference>, <reference osisRef="Luke.14.14">14</reference>).<div eID="gen28235" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen28236" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">mammon of unrighteousness--</hi>treacherous, precarious. (See on <reference osisRef="Matt.6.24">Mt 6:24</reference>).<div eID="gen28236" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen28237" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">ye fail--</hi>in respect of life.<div eID="gen28237" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen28238" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">they may receive you--</hi>not generally, "ye may be received" (as <reference osisRef="Luke.6.38">Lu 6:38</reference>, "shall men give"), but "those ye have relieved may rise up as witnesses for you" at the great day. Then, like the steward, when turned out of one home shall ye secure another; but better than he, a heavenly for an earthly, an everlasting for a temporary habitation. Money is not here made the key to heaven, more than "the deeds done in the body" in general, according to which, as a test of character--but not by the merit of which--men are to be judged (<reference osisRef="2Cor.5.10">2Co 5:10</reference>, and see <reference osisRef="Matt.25.34-Matt.25.40">Mt 25:34-40</reference>). <div eID="gen28238" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv14604"/><div sID="gen28239" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv14604"/><hi type="bold">10. He, &c.--</hi>a maxim of great pregnancy and value; rising from the prudence which the steward had to the fidelity which he had not, the "harmlessness of the dove, to which the serpent" with all his "wisdom" is a total stranger. Fidelity depends not on the amount entrusted, but on the sense of responsibility. He that feels this in little will feel it in much, and conversely. <div eID="gen28239" type="x-p"/>

Son--</hi>stinging acknowledgment of the claimed relationship.<div eID="gen28265" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen28266" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">thou ... Lazarus, &c.--</hi>As it is a great law of God's kingdom, that the nature of our present desires shall rule that of our future bliss, so by that law, he whose "good things," craved and enjoyed, were all bounded by time, could look for none after his connection with time had come to an end (<reference osisRef="Luke.6.24">Lu 6:24</reference>). But by this law, he whose "evil things," all crowded into the present life, drove him to seek, and find, consolation in a life beyond the grave, is by death released from all evil and ushered into unmixed and uninterrupted good (<reference osisRef="Luke.6.21">Lu 6:21</reference>). (<reference osisRef="2Cor.6.2">2</reference>) It is impossible. <div eID="gen28266" type="x-p"/>
